identity.name: AEGIS VOPAK TERMINALS LTD
identity.industry: Energy Logistics / Third-party Liquid & Gas Storage Terminals (LPG, petroleum, chemicals, ammonia)

summary.oneLiner: Aegis Vopak Terminals Ltd is one of India's leading independent liquid and gas storage and terminalling service providers, operating across six key port locations with strong promoter backing from Aegis Logistics and Royal Vopak.
summary.business: AVTL provides safe, reliable liquid and gas storage and terminalling services across six key port locations in India. The company operates through two divisions: Liquid Logistics, handling liquid products, and Gas Terminalling, focused on LPG and ammonia. It serves as a critical infrastructure partner in India's logistics and clean energy supply chain, offering integrated coastal logistics and value-added services.

one-line thesis: First full-year result since IPO: FY26 revenue +17% to INR923 cr, EBITDA +19% to INR687 cr, PAT +52% to INR342 cr as Project GATI capacity (cryogenic LPG at Pipavav & Mangalore, Haldia LPG via Hindustan Aegis acquisition) came online and operating leverage kicked in. The real story is a USD1.2 bn cumulative capex by end-FY27 scaling to a USD5 bn pipeline by 2030 (7 ports → 12 ports), with a deliberate diversification beyond LPG/liquids into ammonia (India's first independent ammonia terminal at Pipavav, anchored by a 15-yr Hindustan Zinc take-or-pay + ITOCHU as strategic partner) — positioning AVTL as the picks-and-shovels infrastructure landlord for India's energy-import growth and the green-hydrogen/energy-transition agenda.

Liquid terminals are billed on an "earning-per-CBM" basis (~INR3,000/CBM is a "very good" blended rate) — physical occupancy is NOT the right KPI; capacity is effectively contracted.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Throughput growth:** ~30–40% YoY throughput growth maintained as the standing guide (no formal earnings guidance given). FY27 expected back on track from Q2 after the Strait-of-Hormuz LPG supply disruption.
- **Capex:** Cumulative capex to reach ~USD1.2 bn by end-FY27 (from ~USD600 m at IPO/FY25). FY28 capex "close to INR5,000 cr." Annual run-rate INR4,000–5,000 cr for next two years, then larger in FY29–30 (post second-phase QIP equity raise) → ~USD5 bn cumulative by end-2030.
- **Commissioning dates (watch slippage):**
  - JNPT Phase-1 liquid (part of 318,100 CBM expansion): commissioning starts ~Jul-2026, "most of it" running in H1 FY27, full 318,000 CBM running ~6 months of the year (some from October). Revenue from Q2 FY27. Mgmt expects high realization from start (JNPA demand strong — no slow ramp).
  - Pipavav: VLGC-compliant jetty by ~mid-FY27/CY-end; petroleum take-or-pay (>0.5 MTPA, 15-yr) ops by year-end FY27; ammonia terminal (36,000 MT) commissioning ~next month (Jul-2026) — "largest cryogenic third-party ammonia terminal in the country."
  - Kandla: CRL4 liquid terminal (+94,148 CBM) on track next year; Kandla–Gorakhpur LPG pipeline H1 FY27; L&T ammonia-terminal MoU progressing to framework agreement.
  - Mangalore–Hassan–Cherlapalli pipeline operative FY28; Mangalore LPG rail gantry earlier.
- **Business mix:** Gas to stay dominant ~55–45 to 60–40 (gas higher) over next 3 years.
order book & pipeline (contracted/take-o:
- **Haldia:** 75% stake in Hindustan Aegis LPG (East Coast LPG entry); anchored by HPCL terminaling agreement through 2038. 226,890 CBM liquid + ~25,000 MT LPG; +3 acres land for expansion.
- **Pipavav petroleum:** 15-yr take-or-pay with "a leading conglomerate," committed volumes >0.5 MTPA — ops by year-end.
- **Pipavav ammonia:** 15-yr take-or-pay with Hindustan Zinc for ~one-third of the 36,000 MT capacity (their upcoming DAP plant, commissioning H1 FY27).
- **Capacity snapshot (CBM liquid / MT LPG):** Kandla ~952,000 / 48,000; JNPT 106,900 (+318,100 building) / +77,236 + 35,000 MTPA bottling; Haldia 226,890; Mangalore 193,000 / 82,000 LPG; Kochi 82,545 (+60,000 planned); Pipavav 70,800 MT LPG total. ~25 operating units across India.
- **Long-dated optionality (MoUs, non-binding):** Vadhvan new port — liquid+gas facilities, ~INR20,000 cr potential outlay (subject to approvals/land); L&T ammonia terminals at Kandla.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Gas terminaling (~52% of FY26 rev):** Cryogenic LPG terminals commissioned at Pipavav (48,000 MT, Jun-2025) and Mangalore (82,000 MT, Jun-2025); Kandla now VLGC-compliant (first VLGC received Dec-2025). Vertically integrated with parent Aegis Logistics' LPG distribution — parent's Q4 distribution volume growth cushioned AVTL terminal utilization during the import disruption.
- **Liquid terminaling (~48% of FY26 rev, fastest grower):** Petroleum + chemical storage; billed per-CBM; Mangalore +75,000 CBM live; JNPT 318,100 CBM expansion (INR1,675 cr) the big near-term driver.
- **Ammonia (new vertical):** Aegis Terminal Pipavav Ltd — India's first independent ammonia terminal; ITOCHU 10%→25%. To be vertically integrated (source-store-distribute) like LPG; same infra usable for green ammonia later. Demand from DAP fertilizer + industrial/specialty-chemical customers.
- **Parent construction model:** All capex built in-house by Aegis Logistics (cost/speed efficiencies) on AVTL-leased land, then owned/operated by AVTL.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Ammonia / green ammonia:** core diversification; mgmt explicitly bullish, plans more ammonia terminals "the moment we digest this first one." Energy-transition / green-H2 aligned.
- **New molecules:** evaluating Ethane, Propylene, natural-gas infrastructure, cryogenic gas tank at JNPT (36,000–50,000 MT, under evaluation).
- **Geographic/format expansion:** 7→12 ports by 2030; inland depots, jetties (backward integration), strategic storage, industrial terminals.
- **Multi-modal evacuation:** Jamnagar–Loni (live), Kandla–Gorakhpur (H1 FY27, 8.25 MMTPA), Bangalore-Hassan-Cherlapalli (later), Uran–Chakan (~1 MT), liquid/LPG rail gantries — raise throughput & efficiency.
margins & cost dynamics:
- EBITDA margin ~74% (FY26 INR686.5 cr on INR923.1 cr) — asset-heavy, high-operating-leverage infrastructure economics; PAT growth (+52%) far outpaced revenue (+17%) as new capacity ramped against largely fixed cost base.
- Liquid: target blended ~INR3,000/CBM earning; occupancy-agnostic (capacity hired out, not volume-contracted).
- Competitive edge claimed on lowest-cost/fastest in-house construction (parent) + Vopak's 400-yr/23-country global ESG-AAA operating standards winning MNC business.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- Cumulative ~USD1.2 bn by end-FY27; INR4,000–5,000 cr/yr run-rate; ~USD5 bn by 2030. Funded via internal accruals + measured debt (target gearing ~0.6x) + a planned second-phase QIP (equity dilution) to fund the back-ended large capex.
- Near-term builds: JNPT 318,100 CBM (INR1,675 cr); Pipavav VLGC jetty + ammonia + rail gantry; Kandla CRL4 (+94,148 CBM); Kochi +60,000 CBM; Mangalore +60,000 CBM (land secured). Vadhvan ~INR20,000 cr (MoU-stage, back-ended optionality).
capital allocation:
- Maiden final dividend INR0.2/sh (~2% on FV) as listed co.
- Disciplined gearing ~0.6x; diversified funding via two NSE-listed NCD series (INR660 cr + INR1,030 cr).
- Reinvestment-heavy phase; equity QIP flagged for FY29-30 leg of the USD5 bn program.
risks & watch-items:
- **LPG import disruption:** Strait-of-Hormuz war (since Mar-2026) cut national-oil-company LPG supply ~50% (Mar), easing to 30–35% (May); normalization expected by Q2 FY27. AVTL partially insulated via parent's distribution integration.
- **Capex execution / back-loading:** USD5 bn is heavily back-ended to FY29-30 and contingent on a future QIP and demand materializing — slippage and equity-dilution risk.
- **MoU-stage optionality:** Vadhvan (INR20,000 cr), L&T Kandla ammonia, JNPT cryo tank — all non-binding/under-evaluation; don't model as committed.
- **Lease tenure:** mostly long-dated; one Pipavav Port concessionaire lease matures 2029 (lessee has "last look" under land policy).
- **Customer/contract structure:** "open-source" model (deliberately low long-term-contract dependence) — flexible but means less locked revenue vs pure take-or-pay peers; offset by 15-yr anchor deals at Haldia/Pipavav.
- **Commissioning timing:** multiple FY27 dates (JNPT Q1-Q2, Pipavav jetty mid-FY27, ammonia ~Jul) to verify.
management quality / tone: - Confident, detailed, candid for a first post-IPO call; Moledina precise on numbers and disciplined-capital framing ("we always follow demand, we are not somebody who will do flag planting"). Chandaria emphasized the Vopak safety/ESG pedigree and ammonia optimism. Mildly promotional on the USD5 bn 2030 vision and Vadhvan, but appropriately hedged ("subject to approvals," "no final decision," "non-binding MoU"). Refused to give formal earnings guidance — only directional throughput growth.
non-obvious takeaways:
- This is a **landlord/toll-road infrastructure** model, not a commodity play — ~74% EBITDA margin, per-CBM "earning" (occupancy-agnostic) on liquids, anchor take-or-pay on gas/ammonia. Volatile LPG import volumes hit throughput optics but the asset economics are insulated by capacity-based billing + parent distribution integration.
- **Ammonia is the real optionality**: first-mover on India's only independent ammonia terminal, Hindustan Zinc DAP anchor + ITOCHU partner + L&T MoU — a direct read-through to India's DAP import-substitution and green-hydrogen/ammonia transition, with the same cryo infra reusable for green ammonia.
- The parent-builds-then-AVTL-owns structure means AVTL captures Aegis Logistics' construction cost efficiency, but related-party capex flow is a governance item to track as the USD5 bn program runs.
- A QIP is effectively pre-announced for the FY29-30 capex leg — dilution is part of the plan, not a surprise risk.

- Near-term builds: JNPT 318,100 CBM (INR1,675 cr); Pipavav VLGC jetty + ammonia + rail gantry; Kandla CRL4 (+94,148 CBM); Kochi +60,000 CBM; Mangalore +60,000 CBM (land secured). Vadhvan ~INR20,000 cr (MoU-stage, back-ended optionality).
capital allocation:
- Maiden final dividend INR0.2/sh (~2% on FV) as listed co.
- Disciplined gearing ~0.6x; diversified funding via two NSE-listed NCD series (INR660 cr + INR1,030 cr).
- Reinvestment-heavy phase; equity QIP flagged for FY29-30 leg of the USD5 bn program.
risks & watch-items:
- **LPG import disruption:** Strait-of-Hormuz war (since Mar-2026) cut national-oil-company LPG supply ~50% (Mar), easing to 30–35% (May); normalization expected by Q2 FY27. AVTL partially insulated via parent's distribution integration.
- **Capex execution / back-loading:** USD5 bn is heavily back-ended to FY29-30 and contingent on a future QIP and demand materializing — slippage and equity-dilution risk.
- **MoU-stage optionality:** Vadhvan (INR20,000 cr), L&T Kandla ammonia, JNPT cryo tank — all non-binding/under-evaluation; don't model as committed.
- **Lease tenure:** mostly long-dated; one Pipavav Port concessionaire lease matures 2029 (lessee has "last look" under land policy).
- **Customer/contract structure:** "open-source" model (deliberately low long-term-contract dependence) — flexible but means less locked revenue vs pure take-or-pay peers; offset by 15-yr anchor deals at Haldia/Pipavav.
- **Commissioning timing:** multiple FY27 dates (JNPT Q1-Q2, Pipavav jetty mid-FY27, ammonia ~Jul) to verify.
management quality / tone: - Confident, detailed, candid for a first post-IPO call; Moledina precise on numbers and disciplined-capital framing ("we always follow demand, we are not somebody who will do flag planting"). Chandaria emphasized the Vopak safety/ESG pedigree and ammonia optimism. Mildly promotional on the USD5 bn 2030 vision and Vadhvan, but appropriately hedged ("subject to approvals," "no final decision," "non-binding MoU"). Refused to give formal earnings guidance — only directional throughput growth.
non-obvious takeaways:
- This is a **landlord/toll-road infrastructure** model, not a commodity play — ~74% EBITDA margin, per-CBM "earning" (occupancy-agnostic) on liquids, anchor take-or-pay on gas/ammonia. Volatile LPG import volumes hit throughput optics but the asset economics are insulated by capacity-based billing + parent distribution integration.
- **Ammonia is the real optionality**: first-mover on India's only independent ammonia terminal, Hindustan Zinc DAP anchor + ITOCHU partner + L&T MoU — a direct read-through to India's DAP import-substitution and green-hydrogen/ammonia transition, with the same cryo infra reusable for green ammonia.
- The parent-builds-then-AVTL-owns structure means AVTL captures Aegis Logistics' construction cost efficiency, but related-party capex flow is a governance item to track as the USD5 bn program runs.
- A QIP is effectively pre-announced for the FY29-30 capex leg — dilution is part of the plan, not a surprise risk.

themes.title: Oil & Gas - gas economy (CGD/LNG) + refining/upstream
themes.need: India's gas-economy push now collides with an outright policy reversal. ATGL grew volume 13% to 303 MMSCM and revenue 27% to INR 1,908cr, yet EBITDA FELL sequentially to INR 281cr (~14.7% margin, from INR 310cr) because the government withdrew the pooled-gas mechanism after the West Asia 'peace deal', pushing ATGL to ~15% spot volumes with Brent above $107/bbl; management also noted NWG price is 12% of the Indian crude basket, so a 62% domestic mix protects far less than it looks, and CNG station adds slowed to +5 from +25 in Q4 even as CNG demand grows ~30%. The same shock ran the other way for integrated refining: RELIANCE delivered O2C EBITDA of INR 17,000cr (+17%) THROUGH the Strait-of-Hormuz closure at 96-97% throughput while Asian peers ran 15-20% below capacity, with ethane+ROGC at ~70% of ethylene feed as distillate cracks blew out (gas oil $16 to $63, ATF $14 to $62). MGL/GUJGASLTD/IGL/IRMENERGY carry the same CGD margin squeeze; PETRONET/OIL/ONGC/IOC ride LNG-infra + domestic-gas; CHENNPETRO/MRPL ride GRM cracks; DEEPINDS/JINDRILL/SEAMECLTD on ONGC E&P capex; AEGISLOG/AEGISVOPAK add LPG/gas terminalling.
themes.driver: Whether the pooled/APM gas-allocation mechanism is restored (the single biggest CGD earnings variable); LNG spot price and Brent; GRM/distillate cracks; ONGC rig tenders & day-rates.

themes.title: Maritime shipping & terminalling
themes.need: Shipping and liquid/gas terminalling players are driven by freight/charter cycles, terminalling tariffs and energy-cargo throughput - not the e-comm/quick-comm/GST-warehousing formalization powering the parcel & 3PL up-cycle.
themes.driver: Freight/charter rates, terminalling tariffs and energy-cargo throughput.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Aegis Vopak Terminals Ltd is one of India's leading independent liquid and gas storage and terminalling service providers, operating across six key port locations with strong promoter backing from Aegis Logistics and Royal Vopak.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: AVTL provides safe, reliable liquid and gas storage and terminalling services across six key port locations in India. The company operates through two divisions: Liquid Logistics, handling liquid products, and Gas Terminalling, focused on LPG and ammonia. It serves as a critical infrastructure partner in India's logistics and clean energy supply chain, offering integrated coastal logistics and value-added services.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Konkan Storage Systems (Kochi) Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary; engaged in terminal/storage operations.
- CRL Terminals Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned material subsidiary; operates specialized storage terminal assets at Kandla (CRL-4/NDDB).
- Aegis Terminal (Pipavav) Limited (ATPL) — subsidiary: Subsidiary w.e.f. November 13, 2025 (96% stake acquired from Aegis Gas (LPG) Private Limited); not yet commenced commercial operations.
- Hindustan Aegis LPG Limited (HALPG) — subsidiary: Material subsidiary w.e.f. January 06, 2026 (51% stake acquired from AGPL, additional stake from Vopak India B.V.); engaged in LPG terminal/storage operations.
- Aegis Logistics Limited (ALL) — related party: Promoter entity; counterparty to Framework Agreements for acquisition of ammonia terminal at Pipavav, Kandla terminal assets, and JNPA greenfield project.
- Sea Lord Containers Limited — related party: Counterparty to Business Transfer Agreement for LPG terminal at New Mangalore Port and Framework Agreement for infrastructure expansion at NMPA.
- Aegis Gas (LPG) Private Limited (AGPL) — related party: Promoter group entity; seller of equity stakes in ATPL and HALPG.
- Vopak India B.V. — related party: Joint venture partner; sold a portion of its stake in HALPG to the Company.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Gas terminaling (~52% of FY26 rev):** Cryogenic LPG terminals commissioned at Pipavav (48,000 MT, Jun-2025) and Mangalore (82,000 MT, Jun-2025); Kandla now VLGC-compliant (first VLGC received Dec-2025). Vertically integrated with parent Aegis Logistics' LPG distribution — parent's Q4 distribution volume growth cushioned AVTL terminal utilization during the import disruption.
- **Liquid terminaling (~48% of FY26 rev, fastest grower):** Petroleum + chemical storage; billed per-CBM; Mangalore +75,000 CBM live; JNPT 318,100 CBM expansion (INR1,675 cr) the big near-term driver.
- **Ammonia (new vertical):** Aegis Terminal Pipavav Ltd — India's first independent ammonia terminal; ITOCHU 10%→25%. To be vertically integrated (source-store-distribute) like LPG; same infra usable for green ammonia later. Demand from DAP fertilizer + industrial/specialty-chemical customers.
- **Parent construction model:** All capex built in-house by Aegis Logistics (cost/speed efficiencies) on AVTL-leased land, then owned/operated by AVTL.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline (contracted/take-or-pay visibility)
order_book.body:
- **Haldia:** 75% stake in Hindustan Aegis LPG (East Coast LPG entry); anchored by HPCL terminaling agreement through 2038. 226,890 CBM liquid + ~25,000 MT LPG; +3 acres land for expansion.
- **Pipavav petroleum:** 15-yr take-or-pay with "a leading conglomerate," committed volumes >0.5 MTPA — ops by year-end.
- **Pipavav ammonia:** 15-yr take-or-pay with Hindustan Zinc for ~one-third of the 36,000 MT capacity (their upcoming DAP plant, commissioning H1 FY27).
- **Capacity snapshot (CBM liquid / MT LPG):** Kandla ~952,000 / 48,000; JNPT 106,900 (+318,100 building) / +77,236 + 35,000 MTPA bottling; Haldia 226,890; Mangalore 193,000 / 82,000 LPG; Kochi 82,545 (+60,000 planned); Pipavav 70,800 MT LPG total. ~25 operating units across India.
- **Long-dated optionality (MoUs, non-binding):** Vadhvan new port — liquid+gas facilities, ~INR20,000 cr potential outlay (subject to approvals/land); L&T ammonia terminals at Kandla.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Throughput growth:** ~30–40% YoY throughput growth maintained as the standing guide (no formal earnings guidance given). FY27 expected back on track from Q2 after the Strait-of-Hormuz LPG supply disruption.
- **Capex:** Cumulative capex to reach ~USD1.2 bn by end-FY27 (from ~USD600 m at IPO/FY25). FY28 capex "close to INR5,000 cr." Annual run-rate INR4,000–5,000 cr for next two years, then larger in FY29–30 (post second-phase QIP equity raise) → ~USD5 bn cumulative by end-2030.
- **Commissioning dates (watch slippage):**
  - JNPT Phase-1 liquid (part of 318,100 CBM expansion): commissioning starts ~Jul-2026, "most of it" running in H1 FY27, full 318,000 CBM running ~6 months of the year (some from October). Revenue from Q2 FY27. Mgmt expects high realization from start (JNPA demand strong — no slow ramp).
  - Pipavav: VLGC-compliant jetty by ~mid-FY27/CY-end; petroleum take-or-pay (>0.5 MTPA, 15-yr) ops by year-end FY27; ammonia terminal (36,000 MT) commissioning ~next month (Jul-2026) — "largest cryogenic third-party ammonia terminal in the country."
  - Kandla: CRL4 liquid terminal (+94,148 CBM) on track next year; Kandla–Gorakhpur LPG pipeline H1 FY27; L&T ammonia-terminal MoU progressing to framework agreement.
  - Mangalore–Hassan–Cherlapalli pipeline operative FY28; Mangalore LPG rail gantry earlier.
- **Business mix:** Gas to stay dominant ~55–45 to 60–40 (gas higher) over next 3 years.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Ammonia / green ammonia:** core diversification; mgmt explicitly bullish, plans more ammonia terminals "the moment we digest this first one." Energy-transition / green-H2 aligned.
- **New molecules:** evaluating Ethane, Propylene, natural-gas infrastructure, cryogenic gas tank at JNPT (36,000–50,000 MT, under evaluation).
- **Geographic/format expansion:** 7→12 ports by 2030; inland depots, jetties (backward integration), strategic storage, industrial terminals.
- **Multi-modal evacuation:** Jamnagar–Loni (live), Kandla–Gorakhpur (H1 FY27, 8.25 MMTPA), Bangalore-Hassan-Cherlapalli (later), Uran–Chakan (~1 MT), liquid/LPG rail gantries — raise throughput & efficiency.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] AVTL acquired a 75% stake in Hindustan Aegis LPG Ltd (HALPG) from Aegis Gas (LPG) Pvt. Ltd. and Vopak India B.V.; board approved 29 Oct 2025 (subject to shareholder approval), Share Purchase Agreement entered 02 January 2026, and HALPG is now a subsidiary of AVTL.
- [Acquisition rationale] HALPG adds a fourth LPG terminal taking total capacity to 225,800 MT, consolidates 25,000 MT of LPG capacity under AVTL (ex-Mumbai), gives East Coast access via the Haldia terminal with integrated storage, terminalling and bottling at one site, and is designed for 2.5 MMT throughput (~100 vessel turnarounds) with an exclusive HPCL agreement till FY 2038.
- [Restatement] FY25 and FY26 numbers are restated due to the consolidation of Hindustan Aegis LPG Ltd (HALPG).
- [Errata] This is a revised presentation: the covering letter states Q1 FY26 Revenue from Gas on slide 6 was corrected from INR 671.46 Mn to INR 1,111.23 Mn.
- [Evacuation infrastructure] LPG facilities connect to the Jamnagar-Loni Pipeline (1,427 km, GAIL, 3.3 MMTPA) and the under-construction Kandla-Gorakhpur Pipeline (2,805 km, described as capable of transporting 25%+ of India's total LPG demand at 8.25 MMTPA and connecting 40+ bottling plants); Pipavav is one of five port-based LPG terminals in India with rail siding, and Pipavav, Kandla and JNPA link to the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor.
